answer: Make each epoch's stamp a verifiable delay function: forge it by a strictly sequential computation no parallel hardware can shorten, seeded fresh when the epoch opens. One identity needs one dedicated lane running the full delta of wall-clock time; a thousand clones need a thousand lanes at once, since sequentiality blocks sharing the chain across seats. You cannot buy an ocean of cores to amortize a chain that must run start to finish — faster chips shave only the margin. Precomputation dies on the fresh seed, so the hardware bill to mint N identities scales linearly with N.
